question: Which charting library should a zero-build, offline-first HTML dossier embed?
title: Chart library selection for offline single-file dossiers
summary: Chart.js is the pick. It is the smallest library that still covers every form the dossier template needs, and its one real weakness — no native accessibility — is already closed by the mandatory table view. ECharts generates better ARIA descriptions but costs roughly five times the bytes for a benefit we get for free elsewhere.

claims.text: Chart.js UMD build is about 208 KB raw, roughly 68 KB gzipped.
ECharts full build is about 1020 KB raw; a custom build trims it but requires a bundler, which the zero-build constraint rules out.
Frappe Charts is about 69 KB raw — the smallest of the three.
Chart.js renders to canvas and ships no native accessibility layer; its documentation directs authors to supply their own fallback content.
ECharts can generate ARIA descriptions from the series data when aria.enabled is set.
Frappe Charts covers bar, line, and percentage forms but has no heatmap or scatter, both of which the dossier template requires.
The dossier template emits a <table> carrying the same numbers for every chart, which is the accessible rendering regardless of the library's own ARIA support.

verdict.rationale: Smallest library that still covers every required form; the accessibility hole is closed by the template's mandatory table view rather than by the library.
verdict.rejected_because: Better generated ARIA, but roughly 5x the bytes for a benefit the table view already delivers.

charts.title: Bundle size, raw
charts.subtitle: Lower is better; zero-baseline preserved so the ratio reads honestly

insights.text: The smallest library is not the cheapest choice: Frappe saves 139 KB but cannot draw two of the required forms, so adopting it means adding a second library and losing the saving.

risks.text: A canvas-rendered chart is invisible to a screen reader without an explicit text equivalent.
risks.mitigation: The template emits role="img" plus aria-label plus a <table> with the same numbers for every chart; grep-verified in the test suite.

recommendations.text: Inline Chart.js in the fallback template and keep the table view mandatory rather than optional.

not_checked.text: Runtime rendering performance at high series counts.
not_checked.reason: Dossiers cap at eight series by design (the dataviz token ceiling), well below where any of the three degrades.

not_checked.text: Long-term maintenance health — release cadence, open-issue trend, bus factor.
not_checked.reason: Out of scope for a single-file embedding decision that is cheap to reverse.

methodology.approach: Direct inspection of each library's distributed bundle plus a read of its published accessibility and feature documentation. No benchmarks were run; the decision turns on size, form coverage, and accessibility, all of which are observable without one.
limitations: Sizes are raw dist bytes, not per-application tree-shaken output.
Accessibility assessed from documentation, not from a screen-reader session.
